core_obligations: Choose an ideal of definition I of A and observe that IC is an ideal of definition of C, because A -> C is adic (proof lines 1522-1524).
Use continuity of B -> C to find an ideal of definition J contained in B whose image lies in IC (proof lines 1524-1526).
Use continuity of A -> B to replace I by the inverse image I' of J inside I, which is again an ideal of definition of A (proof lines 1526-1529).
Sandwich I'C contained in JC contained in IC and conclude that JC is an ideal of definition, so that B -> C is adic (proof lines 1529-1531).
proof_roadmap: Choose an ideal of definition of A and move it to C (proof lines 1522-1524).
Pull an ideal of definition of B back to A and refine I (proof lines 1524-1529).
difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms A -> B -> C of pre-adic rings with A -> C adic, the lemma asserts that B -> C is adic (statement lines 1515-1520). The proof is a displayed sandwiching argument: an ideal of definition I of A is chosen and IC is an ideal of definition of C because A -> C is adic; continuity of B -> C produces an ideal of definition J of B mapping into IC; continuity of A -> B lets one replace I by the inverse image I' of J in I, which is again an ideal of definition; and I'C contained in JC contained in IC sandwiches JC between two ideals of definition, so JC and hence J is an ideal of definition of B with the topology of C being J-adic (proof lines 1522-1531). The level is H2: every move is exhibited, but the argument is a genuine chase through the definition of an adic homomorphism rather than a citation.
